name: Anamarie Lopategui
text: Anamarie Lopategui Started Ogi Deli in Elko on her own Basque side, with sandwiches, and grew it into a pintxo bar.

name: Ansots Basque Chorizos
text: Ansots Basque Chorizos Boise, in the Pioneer Building on West Main. The Ansotegui family's chorizo counter, and a lunch bar beside it. Tuesday to Saturday, ten to three, with evenings by reservation. Chorizo at $10 a pound, small hot plates $9 to $20, a dozen uncooked croquetas $11. The Ansoteguis put down roots in Idaho in the early 1900s. Dan Ansotegui opened Bar Gernika in 1991 and The Basque Market in 1999 before this one. Dan, Tamara and Ellie run it. Chorizos, marinated solomo, Basque bacon over the counter; croquetas, patatas bravas, seafood and meatballs at the bar, with Basque wine and cider. Three of the doors in this directory were opened by the same man. Boise ID Basque chorizos, marinated solomo and Basque bacon, with a lunch counter

name: Artzain
text: Artzain Shepherd. The job that brought the men the boarding houses were built for.

name: Bacalao al pil-pil
text: Bacalao al pil-pil Salt cod, garlic, oil and chilli, worked until the cod's own gelatin turns the oil into a sauce. Four ingredients, no cream. The sauce is an emulsion made by moving the pan, not by adding anything.

name: Bar Gernika
text: Bar Gernika Boise, at Capitol and Grove. A Basque pub on the corner of the Block, five days a week. Named for the town the Luftwaffe bombed in 1937, and for Picasso's painting of it. Boise ID a Basque pub and eatery

name: Baserri
text: Baserri The Basque farmhouse: house, barn, byre and family under one roof, and the unit of inheritance that sent younger sons to America. Primogeniture kept the baserri whole and gave the rest of the children a ticket. That is the mechanism behind every room in this directory.

name: Basque beans
text: Basque beans Small red or pink beans, long-cooked with pork and garlic. On the table at nearly every room in this directory.

name: Basque breakfast
text: Basque breakfast Gardnerville, twice a year, $19 a person plus tax.

name: Basque Museum & Cultural Center
text: Basque Museum & Cultural Center Cyrus Jacobs-Uberuaga House Boise, Grove Street. A boarding house that took Basque men from 1917 to 1969, and has been the country's first Basque museum since 1985. Cyrus Jacobs built the brick house in 1864. Basque families ran it as a boarding house; the Uberuagas took it on in 1917, bought it in 1928, and kept boarders until 1969. Adelia Simplot, a Basque immigrant's daughter, bought it from the family and opened the museum inside it in 1985. Boise ID

name: Basquenese
text: Basquenese Boise, in the Warehouse Food Hall. Basque and Vietnamese in one kitchen, run by a couple who are each half of it. Solomo sandos, croquetas, chorizo hoagies, and noodle soup with herbs. It started as a food truck and took a stall in the hall. Matthew Larrinaga is a fourth-generation Idahoan Basque; Barbie is Vietnamese and cooks from her family's table. The only kitchen in this directory where Basque is one half of a sentence rather than the whole of it. Boise ID a fusion of Vietnamese and Basque street food

name: Benji's French Basque Restaurant
text: Benji's French Basque Restaurant Bakersfield, on Rosedale. French Basque, six days, lunch and dinner with the afternoon shut. Lunch 11:30 to 2, dinner 5 to 9, Tuesday through Sunday. The house asks you to call for a table. Bakersfield CA French Basque

name: Bread pudding
text: Bread pudding The last of the ten courses at Winnemucca, and the house's own.

name: California
text: California Kern County holds more Basque dining rooms than any county in the United States. The rest of the state runs from a members' club in South San Francisco to a tasting counter in West Hollywood.

name: Centro Basco
text: Centro Basco Chino, 1940. A boarding house that still sets a boarders' table one Saturday a month. Dinner comes in separate courses, not all at once. On the last Saturday of the month the house sets the Boarder's Table at 12:30 — one sitting, everyone together, the way the building fed men who worked the dairies. It opened in 1940 as a boarding house for Basque immigrants. Chino CA Basque, from the Pays Basque side of the Pyrenees

name: Chalet Basque
text: Chalet Basque Bakersfield, 1969, on Oak Street. Family style, seven days, and one owner since 2002. Open every day, lunch straight through to dinner. Lisa has run it since 2002. It opened in 1969 and has stood on Oak Street since. Bakersfield CA traditional Basque dishes, family-style

name: Croquetas
text: Croquetas Thick béchamel, set cold, breaded and fried. The pintxo counter's staple.

name: Dan Ansotegui
text: Dan Ansotegui Opened Bar Gernika in 1991, The Basque Market in 1999, and Ansots. Three doors on or beside the Basque Block, from one family that arrived in Idaho in the early 1900s.

name: Dantza
text: Dantza The dances — aurresku danced to greet someone, ezpata-dantza with swords, fandango at the end of the night.

name: Dom's Taverna
text: Dom's Taverna Santa Barbara, on Victoria. Chef Dom Crisp cooks Basque against the Central Coast — seafood, cured meat, farm produce. Dinner every night from five. Bar bites five to six daily, and late ones after nine Tuesday to Saturday. Book through OpenTable. The marble bar came out of a decommissioned church and was put back together with kintsugi — the breaks gilded rather than hidden. Santa Barbara CA Basque-inspired coastal cooking, drawing on Spain's Basque Country and the California Central Coast

name: Epi's, a Basque Restaurant
text: Epi's, a Basque Restaurant Meridian, 1999. A family restaurant named for a woman born in Bizkaia in 1903. Five nights, dinner only, five to eight. The house asks you to call or text. Founded by the descendants of Maria Epifania Lamiquis-Inchausti — Epi — born 4 February 1903 in Bizkaia. Lamb shank as a standing special; solomo, marinated pork loin with pimentos, in a sandwich. Meridian ID Basque

name: Etxe
text: Etxe House. The Cincinnati room took it for a name.

name: Euskara
text: Euskara The language. Related to nothing else living — not to Spanish, not to French, not to anything in the Indo-European family.

name: Garlic fried chicken
text: Garlic fried chicken The cheapest dinner on the Wool Growers list at $22, and the one people drive for.

name: Glendora Continental Restaurant
text: Glendora Continental Restaurant Glendora, on Route 66, 1980. Jean and Elisabeth Sabarots came from the Basque Country; she had worked in a hotel there. Lunch and dinner six days, bar until two in the morning every day. Bingo on Tuesday, karaoke on Wednesday, a band on Friday and Saturday, an open jam on Sunday night. The only room in this directory whose bar runs later than its kitchen by twelve hours. Glendora CA Basque, by way of a hotel kitchen in the Basque Country

name: Gâteau basque
text: Gâteau basque Two discs of short pastry around pastry cream or black-cherry jam, baked in a tin and often scored with a lauburu. It belongs to Lapurdi and the French side. American Basque rooms mostly end dinner with ice cream or a bread pudding instead.

name: Idaho
text: Idaho One city block in Boise carries more Basque life than any other address in the United States — a museum in a boarding house, a bar, a market, a dining room, a club, and a festival that brings 30,000 people every five years.

name: Idiazabal
text: Idiazabal Hard sheep's-milk cheese from Latxa and Carranzana ewes, often smoked. The shepherd's own product. The same animal, and the same trade, that brought Basque men to Nevada and Idaho.

name: Ikurriña
text: Ikurriña Red ground, white cross over a green saltire. Designed in 1894; flown over American Basque clubs since long before it was legal at home.

name: J.T. Basque Bar and Dining Room
text: J.T. Basque Bar and Dining Room Gardnerville. A building hauled from Virginia City in 1896; the Lekumberry family since April Fool's Day, 1960. Communal long tables, dishes passed down the row. The house calls the Picon Punch a mandatory beginning to a Basque dinner. The J.T. in the name is the initials of the owners who put it up in 1955. The Lekumberrys bought it on 1 April 1960. In the 1960s lunch was $1.25 and dinner $1.50. Gardnerville NV Basque, family style, multi-course

name: Jaialdi
text: Jaialdi Boise, every five years, six days. Between 30,000 and 50,000 people. Last held 29 July to 3 August 2025; next in 2030. Jaialdi is festival in Euskara.

name: Jose Mari Artiach
text: Jose Mari Artiach Came from the Basque Country to herd sheep, and opened Leku Ona on the Basque Block in December 2005.

name: Kalimotxo
text: Kalimotxo Red wine and cola, half and half, over ice. The festival drink. Unlike the Picon Punch, this one is drunk in the Basque Country too — it is said to have been mixed at a Basque festival in the 1970s.

name: Lamb chops
text: Lamb chops The sheepherder's own animal, and the most-priced dish across this directory.

name: Lauburu
text: Lauburu Four comma-shaped heads turning around a centre. Cut into gravestones, chests, cheese rinds and pastry lids. It is carved on Basque graves in Idaho as readily as in Bizkaia.

name: Leku Ona
text: Leku Ona Boise, the Basque Block, December 2005. A dining room with a hotel over it, two patios, and a bar that runs to midnight. Kitchen to 10, bar to midnight, six days. Booking through Resy. Happy hour Tuesday to Saturday, 4 to 6. Jose Mari Artiach came from the Basque Country as a sheepherder and opened it in December 2005. Leku ona is good place in Euskara — the same two words as Toki Ona in Elko, said another way. Boise ID Basque

name: Louis Erreguible
text: Louis Erreguible Opened Louis' Basque Corner in Reno with Lorraine Erreguible in 1967.

name: Louis' Basque Corner
text: Louis' Basque Corner Reno, 1967. Family style at the corner of Fourth and Evans, and it says so about the Picon. Dinner is family style — shrimp and tongue Basquaise, oxtails, tripas callos, lamb chops, sirloin. The banquet room holds 125. Louis and Lorraine Erreguible opened it in 1967, ten blocks from where Reno's Basque hotels stood. Reno NV Basque, family style

name: Maria Epifania Lamiquis-Inchausti
text: Maria Epifania Lamiquis-Inchausti Epi Born 4 February 1903 in Bizkaia. Her descendants opened Epi's in Meridian in 1999 and named it for her.

name: Marmitako
text: Marmitako Tuna, potato, onion, pepper — the pot a Bay of Biscay crew cooked on board, now a festival competition ashore. Named for the marmita, the pot. Ondarroa and Algorta run contests for it.

name: Michelle Anchustegui
text: Michelle Anchustegui The Triangle in Sweet, Idaho cooks her dishes; her family keeps them on the menu.

name: Mus
text: Mus The card game. Four players, two pairs, bidding in four rounds, and signals across the table that everyone can see and nobody is supposed to. Friday nights in Elko you can watch it or sit in. NABO runs a mus tournament across its clubs.

name: Nevada
text: Nevada Hotels built beside the tracks to feed sheepherders, still setting the long table. In 2025 the state made the Picon Punch its official cocktail.

name: Noriega Hotel
text: Noriega Hotel Noriega's Bakersfield, 1893–2020, then 2021–2025. Closed twice. The bar and the neon sign are in a museum. Nothing serves under this name. The Sumner Street building stands empty. One seating, one bell, one price, whatever the kitchen cooked that day, at a table you shared. The James Beard Foundation named it an America's Classic in 2011. It closed in 2020. New owners reopened a Noriega's on Stockdale Highway in June 2021 with the old recipes and the old chairs; that closed in early 2025. The bar and the neon went to the Kern County Museum. Bakersfield CA Basque boarding-house table, one seating, set menu

name: North American Basque Organizations
text: North American Basque Organizations NABO The federation of Basque clubs in North America. Its member roster is the clearest map of where Basque America organized itself. Read 16 September 2026: clubs in California, Colorado, Idaho, Nevada, New York, Oregon, Rhode Island, Utah, Washington, Wyoming, the District of Columbia, British Columbia, Quebec and Saint-Pierre-et-Miquelon.

name: Ogi Deli
text: Ogi Deli Ogi Deli, Bar & Pintxos Elko, 460 Commercial Street. Bread all day, and on Thursday and Friday nights the only pintxo-pote in this directory — a pintxo and a pint for $5. Deli hours are weekday mornings and lunch. Then twice a week the room turns into a bar: pintxos out on the counter, Basque cider on tap, and from 4:30 to 6 a pintxo with a pote — a pint of beer, a glass of house wine, or a glass of sagardoa — for $5 the pair. On Fridays you can watch or play mus. Anamarie Lopategui started it on her own Basque side, with sandwiches. In December 2016 it moved into a restored historic building at 460 Commercial Street and grew a pintxo counter and a bar. Choch Goicoechea and Carolyn took it on in October 2022. Basque chorizo on a French roll. A lamb sandwich. Pintxos on skewers. Imported sagardoa, patxaran, Basque wine, craft beer on tap. Ogi is bread in Euskara. The name is the shortest statement of purpose in this directory. Elko NV delicious, handcrafted Basque and American sandwiches, salads, pintxos (Basque tapas) and drinks — served in a beautifully restored historic building

name: Ormachea's
text: Ormachea's Winnemucca, on Melarkey, since 1978. A Basque-inspired steakhouse where family style starts at six people. Dinner only, Tuesday to Saturday, four to nine. Every entree carries soup or salad and Basque beans. The clearest published seating rule in this directory: your own table for two, the long one for six. Winnemucca NV a Basque-inspired steakhouse

name: Ostatua
text: Ostatua The boarding house. Every old room in this directory was one first. A bed, a meal, a place to leave your money and your mail, and someone who spoke Euskara. The restaurant is the part that survived.

name: Oxtail stew
text: Oxtail stew A boarding-house cut cooked long. $30 at Wool Growers; on the family-style list at Louis'.

name: Patxaran
text: Patxaran Sloes steeped in anise spirit until it turns rose-brown. Sweet, taken cold after dinner. On the back bar in Elko, which is not a common sight in the United States.

name: Pickled tongue
text: Pickled tongue Beef tongue, brined and sliced thin, on the relish tray at the Bakersfield rooms.

name: Picon Punch
text: Picon Punch Bitter orange amer, a spoon of grenadine, soda, a float of brandy, a lemon twist. Basque America's drink, and not a Basque Country one. Nevada made it the official state cocktail in 2025. Ask for one in Bilbao and nobody will know what you mean. It appears to have been put together in the American West, most likely San Francisco, in the last years of the 1800s — Amer Picon had just reached the coast, Gold Rush bar culture was running, and Basque boarding houses took it up as a house pour. One of the earliest printed versions is in the second edition of William Boothby's American Bartender, San Francisco, 1900, filed simply as Amer Picon.

name: Pilota
text: Pilota The handball game, played against a wall. Every Basque town has a fronton; so do Boise and Elko.

name: Pintxo
text: Pintxo A single bite on a slice of bread, held with a stick. A bar counter's unit of measure. Spelled pincho in Spanish and pintxo in Euskara. Which spelling a sign uses says where the room is looking.

name: Pintxo-pote
text: Pintxo-pote A pintxo and a pote — one drink — taken together, at a fixed price, in a fixed hour. Elko keeps one on Thursday and Friday, 4:30 to 6, at $5. In the Basque Country it is a whole town's habit: a street of bars, one pintxo and one small drink at each, moving on. Elko does it in one room.

name: Pyrenees Café
text: Pyrenees Café Bakersfield, 1901. A boarding house by the rail yard that never stopped feeding people. It opens for breakfast, which almost no Basque dining room does, and runs through to a late bar. It went up near the Bakersfield train station in 1901 and took in Basque men who arrived by rail and left for the hills with a flock. The boarders are gone; the long tables stayed. Bakersfield CA Basque, out of a boarding house

name: Sagardoa
text: Sagardoa Dry Basque cider, still, poured thin from a height so it breaks on the glass. Elko imports it. In a sagardotegi it comes straight from the barrel when someone calls txotx.

name: Sagardotegi
text: Sagardotegi A cider house: barrels along one wall, txotx called when a barrel is opened, cod omelette and a beef chop at a shared table standing up.

name: Santa Fe Basque Restaurant
text: Santa Fe Basque Restaurant Fresno, on Maroa. A small family house that keeps two standing dates: a chicken-liver dinner the second Thursday of the month, and a Basque breakfast. Noon to seven Monday and Tuesday, noon to eight Wednesday to Saturday, shut Sunday. Reservations help them staff the night. The chicken-liver dinner comes as soup, salad, potato salad with shrimp, chicken livers with gravy, fried chicken, wine and dessert. The Basque breakfast is eggs, bacon, chorizo, biscuits and gravy, potatoes, pancakes, cheese and wine. Fresno CA a small, family-owned and operated business

name: Solomo
text: Solomo Pork loin marinated with pimentos, served in a sandwich. Boise's own counter food.

name: Somni
text: Somni West Hollywood. Twenty courses from Aitor Zabala, who cooked at elBulli. The most expensive table in Los Angeles, and the only three-star one in this directory. A counter, a tasting menu, and a drinks pairing you cannot decline. Reported at $645 a head on relaunch and $745 to $785 with the mandatory pairing; pairings run $150 for mocktails, $190 half and half, and $225, $415 or $1,000 for wine. Euskal Kazeta files it under Basque and Catalan. It belongs to the same directory as a $5 pintxo in Elko, and the distance between those two numbers is the point of printing both. West Hollywood CA Basque and Catalan

name: Talo
text: Talo A flat maize cake cooked on iron, folded around chistorra or cheese. Bread before wheat bread. Sold hot at markets and festivals; the iron it is cooked on is a museum object in its own right.

name: Taylor's Café
text: Taylor's Café Chino, on Chino Avenue. Weekday mornings only — a Basque and Mexican counter with a full bar. Seven to three, Monday to Friday, shut at the weekend. Bread comes out with whipped butter and salsa, which is the whole story of this room in one plate. Chino CA Basque and Mexican, with a full bar

name: The Basque Block
text: The Basque Block Grove Street between Sixth and Capitol, Boise. A pub, a market, a dining room, a club and a museum — and the museum is the boarding house all of it came out of.

name: The Basque Market
text: The Basque Market Boise, on Grove. A shop with a pintxo counter and paella cooked outside twice a week. Paella Wednesdays and Fridays at noon, first Thursdays at 6. Walk up, order, eat on the patio or carry it off. Pintxo Hour keeps the door open to 6 on Thursday, Friday and Saturday. It is a market that feeds people, not a dining room. Two people can eat here without sitting down. Boise ID pintxos, paella, Spanish and Basque wine, a deli

name: The bitter has a supply problem
text: The bitter has a supply problem Nevada made the Picon Punch its state cocktail in 2025 — the year the American bitter it is built on stopped being made. No factory closed: the recipe was given away, to Reno.

name: The Boarder's Table
text: The Boarder's Table Chino, the last Saturday of the month, 12:30. One sitting, everyone at it. Centro Basco sets it the way the building fed the men who lived upstairs.

name: The Brass Rail
text: The Brass Rail Alturas, Modoc County, on Lakeview Drive. Family style, five courses, a wood fire and a jukebox — and a Picon at the bar. The furthest north-east room in this directory, a long way from any other. A regular names the french fries here as the best of any room in it. Five courses before the entree: bread and butter, soup, salad, the day's dish, then what you ordered, with wine, coffee and ice cream after. Alturas CA family-style Basque

name: The Lekumberry family
text: The Lekumberry family Bought the J.T. in Gardnerville on 1 April 1960 and have run it since.

name: The long table
text: The long table You booked dinner for two. The house seats you with four strangers and brings everyone the same nine dishes. This directory counts which rooms do that, and leaves the verdict to you.

name: The Maitia family
text: The Maitia family J.B. and Mayie Maitia opened Wool Growers in 1954; their daughter Jenny and granddaughter Christiane run it.

name: The Martin Hotel
text: The Martin Hotel Winnemucca, 1898. Built by the railroad to feed sheepherders; still serving the full set dinner. Every dinner carries the same long tail of courses, whatever the entree. It went up in 1898 beside the tracks, and took in Basque men working sheep in the Humboldt country. Winnemucca NV Basque tradition, full set dinner

name: The Picon glass
text: The Picon glass Georgian Irish coffee glass Libbey 8054 Northern Nevada pours a Picon into a six-ounce stemmed glass. One of them you can order this afternoon. The other has a name, a town, and a trail that goes cold in 2015. Outside northern Nevada the drink lands in a highball or a Collins, which changes the proportions more than people admit — the stem glass holds six ounces, and a Collins holds twice that.

name: The relish tray
text: The relish tray What lands before you have ordered anything: pickled tongue, salsa, beans, bread, and it keeps coming back. It is not an appetiser you choose. It arrives because you sat down, and it is refilled without being asked for. Two people who order one entree between them will still be fed.

name: The set dinner
text: The set dinner Not a menu. A sequence the house serves whatever you ordered — soup, salad, beans, potatoes, a side, a vegetable, bread, fries, dessert. The Martin Hotel prints its own, in order: a glass of wine, homemade soup, salad, Basque beans, mashed potatoes, a Basque side dish, a vegetable, home-baked bread, hand-cut fries, Martin bread pudding. The entree you chose is one line in a meal of eleven.

name: The Star Hotel
text: The Star Hotel The Star Hotel & Bar Elko, 1910. Family style, six days a week, on Silver Street. Lunch and dinner run straight through from 11 to 9:30; the bar keeps going after the kitchen stops. Cabbage soup, Basque beans, salad and bread come to the table before the order does. Elko NV Basque dining, family style

name: The Triangle
text: The Triangle Sweet, Gem County, on Highway 52. Friday to Sunday only, and Basque because of one family. Friday eleven to ten, Saturday eight to ten, Sunday eight to nine. Aaron Lowe runs it. The Basque cooking here carries on from Michelle Anchustegui, through her family and the dishes she made. Chorizo is on now; the house has said paella and more are coming. Sweet ID Basque dishes in a country restaurant

name: Toki Ona
text: Toki Ona Elko, on Idaho Street, since 1990. Family-run, family style, and open from six in the morning to half past nine at night, seven days. The longest opening hours of any room in this directory. Breakfast through dinner, every day. Homemade soups, Caesar salads, baked potatoes, served family style. Toki ona is good place in Euskara — the same two words as Leku Ona in Boise, said the other way round. Elko NV family-style Basque

name: Txakoli
text: Txakoli Sharp, barely fizzy white from the Basque coast, poured from a height so it opens in the glass. Almost none of the Western rooms in this directory list it. It arrives with the newer city rooms.

name: Txistu
text: Txistu A three-holed flute played with the left hand while the right beats a drum. One musician, two instruments.

name: Txoko
text: Txoko A members' cooking society — a kitchen a group keeps and cooks in for itself.

name: Txuleta
text: Txuleta A thick bone-in beef chop over wood. The dish the Cincinnati room is built around. No Western room in this directory lists it. It came with the newer restaurants, from the asadors of Gipuzkoa and Bizkaia rather than from the sheep camps.

name: Villa Basque Café and Deli
text: Villa Basque Café and Deli Carson City, on a street called Basque Way. Pete and Martha Coscarart's counter, and the home of Pete's chorizo. Kitchen six to half past two, Tuesday to Saturday; the chorizo shop stays open to four. Pete's Basque chorizo started in Battle Mountain in 1984 and came south with them. Two businesses in one door: a café you sit down in, and a sausage counter you leave with a bag from. Carson City NV Basque deli and café — home of Pete's chorizo

name: Wool Growers Restaurant
text: Wool Growers Restaurant Woolgrowers Bakersfield, 1954. The Maitia family's dining room behind a cocktail lounge on East 19th. Three generations of one family have run it: J.B. and Mayie Maitia opened in 1954, their daughter Jenny took it on, and Jenny's daughter Christiane works it now. The bar takes walk-ins; a table is a phone call ahead. A relish tray lands first — pickled tongue, salsa, beans, bread — and keeps landing. The entree is what you ordered; the rest of the meal is not. Bakersfield CA Basque, in the sheepherder line, with a French Basque hand

name: Wool Growers Restaurant
text: Wool Growers Restaurant Los Banos, on H Street. Family style, six days, and by its own account more than a hundred years old. Private dining rooms, wine, and a book-by-email reservation. Same name as the Bakersfield room, a different house. The house describes uniforms, artwork and family-style service; it does not publish its hours day by day. Los Banos CA family-style Basque

name: Zazpi at the Basque Cultural Center
text: Zazpi at the Basque Cultural Center Basque Cultural Center South San Francisco. A club dining room, renovated, open to anyone who walks in. The Basque Cultural Center is a members' club; its restaurant, now called Zazpi, serves the public lunch and dinner six days a week. Zazpi is seven in Euskara — the seven Basque provinces, the same count in the Zazpiak Bat motto. South San Francisco CA Basque

name: Zazpiak Bat
text: Zazpiak Bat Seven provinces, one people. The motto, and the name of clubs from Reno to Vancouver.
